description: Create a standing rule that categorizes matching transactions into a category, now and on every future import. **This is the widest write here** — it reaches the whole history — so it needs two calls: the first returns the transactions the rule would match plus a confirmation token, and the second must quote that token back. Show the user the matches before you commit; the token expires the moment the match set changes. Rows categorized by hand are never touched.

account_id.description: Restrict the rule to one account.

amount_max.description: Restrict by amount, as a magnitude in major units.

amount_min.description: Restrict by amount, as a magnitude in major units.

apply_to_existing.description: Default true: also categorize the transactions it already matches. False creates the rule for future imports only.

category_id.description: The category the rule assigns. Ids come from `category_tree`.

commit.description: Default false. True requires `confirmation` from the preview.

confirmation.description: The token the preview printed. Required to commit.

kind.description: One of EXACT_MERCHANT, CONTAINS, REGEX, PROVIDER_CATEGORY, AMOUNT_RANGE, ACCOUNT. Default CONTAINS, which survives the branch numbers and spacing that vary between two statements of the same shop.

name.description: Optional. Defaults to the pattern, which is the name of most rules.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

pattern.description: What the rule matches on. Required for every kind but ACCOUNT and AMOUNT_RANGE.

name: create_rule
title: Create a categorization rule
